physical_harm: Deceased was found in a pool of blood with injuries to the mouth and nose, and was declared dead
number_of_offences: Charged under Section 302, convicted under Section 304 Part II
key_evidence_accepted: The evidence brought on record established that there was a farewell party, the appellant fought with another army official, the deceased intervened and was abused by the appellant, the deceased was found in a pool of blood, and the appellant surrendered at the police station. The confessional statement made by the appellant was voluntary and supported by the testimony of witnesses.
witness_credibility: The testimony of witnesses stood firm during cross-examination. The confessional statement made by the appellant was voluntary and supported by the testimony of witnesses.
post_offence_conduct: The appellant surrendered at the police station and stated that he had stabbed one person with a knife.

legal_representation.state: R. Balasubramaniam, Amarendra Bal, Vikas Malhotra, B.V. Bairam Das and Anil Katiyar

investigation_status: FIR lodged, charge sheet filed, trial completed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant was present in the room, had indulged in an altercation, was in a drunken state, and was alone in the room. The chain of circumstances was complete, and the appellant's presence at the police station and absence at the 'fall in parade' were against him. The confessional statement made by the appellant was voluntary and supported by the testimony of witnesses.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the evidence contained discrepancies, the presence of other persons in the room was possible, and the non-recovery of the knife undermined the prosecution case. They also contended that the tribunal failed to analyze the discrepancies and relied on hearsay evidence, making the judgment perverse.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the circumstances from which the conclusion of guilt is sought to be established must be conclusive in nature. The court emphasized that the chain of circumstances must be consistent only with the hypothesis of the appellant's guilt.
precedent_relied_upon: Hema v. State 2013 (3) SCR 1; Union of India v. Major Rabinder Singh 2011 (15) SCR 793; Appabhai v. State of Gujarat AIR 1988 SC 696; Rohtash Kumar v. State of Haryana 2013 (3) SCR 884; Bachan Singh v. Union of India 2008 (10) SCR 668; Gilbert Pereira v. State of Karnataka AIR 2004 12 SCC 281; Ravindran v. Superintendent of Customs (2007) 6 SCC 410; Rumi Bora Dutta v. State of Assam (2013) 7 SCC 417
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence of seven years of rigorous imprisonment was imposed because the accused should be aware of the consequences of his actions, and although he did not intend to kill, the injury caused was likely to result in death. The court found him guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304 Part II of the IPC.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The appellant had indulged in an altercation in the party, was in a drunken state, was alone present in the room, and had escaped by the rear door. His presence at the police station and absence at the 'fall in parade' were aggravating factors.
